articles.title: ‘I was too scared to stop’: Gurgaon biker recounts chase and crash on GCR
articles.summary: Gurgaon road rage: Woman biker Shivani Chauhan says a Maruti Ciaz chased and hit her on Golf Course Road. Accused arrested; police add attempt to murder, stalking charges.
articles.body: GURGAON: “I was very scared, so I did not stop.”Two days after a Maruti Ciaz chased and hit her on Golf Course Road, throwing her off her Aprilia and into the path of speeding traffic, Shivani Chauhan told TOI she never wanted a confrontation — she only wanted to get away.Shivani (27) said the ordeal began when the car came dangerously close to her motorcycle. The car first swept past her at high speed. “I thought, maybe, he had not seen me or was in a hurry. But if you have gone that fast, then go straight ahead. What sense does it make to stop ahead, gesture at me, then hit me from behind and run away?” she asked.Shivani said the car’s occupants repeatedly asked her to stop. “There were four boys in the vehicle. They were, perhaps, drunk and kept chasing me. They wanted to say something, but I did not want to talk,” she added.Shivani said she slowed to around 50-60kmph as the car moved across her path. She estimated it was travelling at around 100kmph or more when it came alongside and struck her. She was flung onto the road as her motorcycle skidded away, sparks flying from the friction.She suffered bruises and injuries to her knee and hand, but said the protective gear prevented fractures or worse. “I thank God that I had my riding shoes and gloves. The way my hand hit the road made me realise what could have happened. I could have broken my shoulder or legs.”The incident was captured on the camera mounted on her bike. Another camera also recorded the car moving across lanes before the collision.But one question still haunts her. What if the timing had been slightly different? “What if there had been a difference of two or three seconds? I could have suffered much deeper injuries, my bones could have broken, or I could have died on the spot,” she said.The Ciaz sped away after the crash. One of Shivani’s friends chased it and caught up with it at a traffic signal, but Shivani said the driver denied responsibility and left again. The accused, Kalyan Bainsla (33), later gave a media interview, claiming a group of bikers had been riding aggressively and that Shivani suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn. He denied hitting her deliberately.Shivani rejected the version. “If you felt so bad for me, why did you not stop at that time?” she asked, questioning why nobody checked on her after the collision.Police subsequently arrested Bainsla in Rajasthan along with his cousin Lovneesh (32), who was also in the car. DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said police added Section 109 of BNS, for attempt to murder, after analysing the footage and added that the collision appeared deliberate. Sections 78 and 79, relating to stalking and insulting a woman’s modesty, were also added after Shivani’s statement.For Shivani, the incident is about more than one dangerous ride. “Every woman rider should be able to feel safe on the city’s roads. Unfortunately, that sense of security is still missing,” she said.Sunday was meant to be a simple escape from her routine of helping residents in Kalkaji with civic problems. Her father Roshan Chauhan, an AAP functionary, said she had bought her first motorcycle only five to six months ago. “Her Sunday routine was simple. She wanted to ride out, have tea and return home,” he added.Shivani had gone out with a group of bikers on Sept 13. The family learnt about the crash only the next day, when journalists reached their home.Shivani, a fashion designing graduate, contested the 2022 MCD election on an AAP ticket at 23 and finished second. articles.title: ‘She is in a lot of pain, has hidden bruises’: Gurgaon biker’s father; Sia to undergo MRI, X-rays today
articles.summary: GURGAON: The woman biker injured in the Gurgaon Golf Course Road hit-and-run case will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospit.
articles.body: GURGAON: The woman biker injured in the Gurgaon Golf Course Road hit-and-run case will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospital, her father said, as she continued to experience pain from injuries sustained in the collision.Her father said Sia was in considerable pain and that some injuries may become apparent only later.He said she had several hidden bruises following the incident and would visit a hospital in Delhi on Wednesday for X-rays, MRIs and whatever treatment she requires.“After an injury, you often discover later where you have actually been hurt, such as hidden bruises, and she had quite a few of those,” Sia’s father told news agency ANI.Sia also said she was in pain and would undergo further medical tests for some of her injuries. “MLC has been done. For a few injuries, MRI tests and X-ray have to be done,” she told news agency ANI.Sia says she was chased, deliberately hitSia alleged that the accused and others in the car had harassed her before the collision and deliberately rammed into her vehicle.“Whatever happened to me on Sunday morning was recorded on my video. I have told the Magistrate what I faced personally. I was chased, harassed, and intentionally hit; I could have died,” she added.She said she had given her statement before the magistrate and requested the strictest action in the case.Haryana Police have arrested primary accused Kalyan Bainsla from Dausa, Rajasthan, along with co-occupant Lovneesh from Palwal, after they allegedly fled the scene and switched off their phones.Sia and her family have maintained that the collision on Golf Course Road was an intentional attack and not an accident.Her father also described the incident as an attempt to murder and thanked police for arresting the accused.‘Not hit-and-run, but attempt to murder’: Sia’s advocateSia's advocate, Abhishek, said the case was registered under attempted murder provisions based on the manner in which the vehicle hit her and the accused fled the spot."The charges that have been filed are for attempted murder. As is evident from the video, this is not a hit-and-run case; it is an attempt to murder case. Of course, one cannot comment conclusively on the specific intent of the accused at this stage. That is something the investigation will establish. However, the manner in which the victim was struck and the accused then fled the scene raises serious questions and, on that basis, the case has been registered as attempted murder rather than merely a hit-and-run incident," he told news agency ANI.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Plans to build massive solar farm in Wiltshire edge closer
articles.summary: More than 5,000 people have objected to plans for the 500-megawatt solar farm in North Wiltshire.
articles.body:
The next stage of the planning process for what could be one of the UK's biggest solar farms has begun.

More than 5,000 people have objected to Island Green Power plans to build a 500-megawatt solar farm across 3,000 acres in North Wiltshire and now the final set of public hearings have started as part of a six month examination period.

Anna-Kate Fuller, founder of the campaign group Stop Lime Down, said: "We have worked tirelessly to raise funds from across our community to protect and preserve this part of the countryside."

Will Threlfall, Senior Project Development Manager responded: "We will continue to listen carefully and respond to the points raised throughout the process".

There are several other larger scale sites in the planning process, including one at Botley in Oxfordshire .

Getting a decision on this is a long process, the original application was submitted in September 2025, then the public were invited to have their say.

The plans are now in an examination stage, where any interested or affected parties can share views and evidence about the plans and the examining authority asks questions about the proposals.

The evidence submitted is wide ranging - from the potential impact on individual land owners and businesses, to established wildlife habitats and farming practices on the land in question.

This stage finishes on October 21st, at which point the examining authority have up to three months to make a recommendation about whether or not the scheme should go ahead.

After that, it could be another three months until a decision is made in Spring 2027.

articles.title: Ryder Cup 2027: Team Europe stars give verdict on early trip to Adare Manor and 'fresh energy' for Luke Donald's side
articles.summary: Team Europe enjoyed a practice round at Adare Manor on Monday ahead of the Ryder Cup being hosted there next September; Several members of Luke Donald's side discussed the benefits of the team trip in their BMW PGA Championship press conferences
articles.body:
Although not quite a full scouting mission like Donald provided ahead of previous Ryder Cup wins at Marco Simone GC and Bethpage Black, it gave many of his potential players an early experience of tackling next year's Ryder Cup venue in Ireland.

A mix of established Ryder Cup members and likely rookie contenders made the trip after the Amgen Irish Open, with a team dinner followed by 18 holes on Monday

Sixteen players joined Donald and his vice-captains for the team session ahead of travelling onto the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - 10 of last year's line-up, two more with past Ryder Cup pedigree and four potential debutants.

"Any time I'm asked to go to Adare Manor, I'm going to go happily and willingly," said Jon Rahm. "It's one of the best hotel golf course experiences there is in the world.

"It was a lot of fun. It was very enjoyable. I think those days are great for all of us to see each other and just in a way remember why we do what we do.

"For those players who have never been there before, I think it's just getting those first nerves out of the way of how they may feel.

Only Rory McIlroy and Rasmus Hojgaard were missing from Donald's dozen that celebrated a 15-13 victory in New York. Alex Noren - a winner in 2018 and vice-captain last year - and Nicolai Hojgaard, part of the 2023 team, also made the trip.

Alex Fitzpatrick and Kristoffer Reitan both featured after impressive rookie campaigns on the PGA Tour, while Spanish duo Eugenio Chacarra and Ángel Ayora were the other newcomers involved.

Most travelled straight from the Amgen Irish Open, with Shane Lowry a later arrival after his record-breaking 11-shot win on home soil at Trump International Golf Links.

"It was a lovely boys' day out, in the sense we got together and had a nice dinner," Justin Rose told the Sky Sports podcast . "There was some intention-setting of what it means to be on the team and what the plans are going forward.

"The round itself yesterday was very casual, very fun and just a first look at the golf course. Having Adare Manor pretty much to yourself is a pretty special experience.

"For them [rookies], it lights the fire even more in them to want to be a part of that team. It gives them the comfort to feel like they're already part of the team, in the sense of [being in] Luke's thoughts, the way of doing things and how the captain goes about it.

"It doesn't necessarily feel like a game-changing trip and 'wow, we have an advantage' or anything like that, but I think it's very important in terms of culture setting and all that."

The European players went out in groups of four for a round in calm conditions, with some playing the course for the first time and others refamiliarizing themselves with a venue that previously hosted the JP McManus Pro-Am.

"With the good weather they've had in Europe, in Ireland, it was in as good a shape as I've ever seen it," Rahm added. "It was actually firm. They could have had it as fast as they wanted to.

"It wasn't overly fast because obviously I think they want the public to still enjoy the week. It was in perfect condition. It was immaculate."

The last two Ryder Cups in Europe have been on venues used for regular DP World Tour events, with Le Golf National (2018) a past site of the Open de France and Marco Simone GC (2023) the Open d'Italia, giving Donald a different challenge in Ireland.

"The strategy around setting up the course is very different from when they have a lot of data from the [DP World] Tour," Noren explained. "It's a very difficult task to set that up, I think, to our advantage. We'll see how they do.

"It's the course and the resources where you can set it up pretty much however you want - you can grow in the rough, you can expand, and you can use tee boxes. It's like not particularly a blank sheet of paper, but you can do whatever you want."

Who else was missing and what happens next?

PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai was invited but unable to attend due to a close friend's wedding in Portugal on Sunday, while Tom McKibbin - who played two rounds with Donald in Ireland last week - was not involved.

Ryder Cup qualification is already under way, with points only available via the Race to Dubai standings for the rest of this season before including FedExCup points in January, with Rose expecting to see some new editions in Team Europe next September.

"I think freshening it up a little bit would be a good thing," Rose admitted. "You want your team to be experienced but to have some fresh energy is always great. Whether that be ideas, style of game, pairing options - to change is up is a good thing.

"There's plenty of opportunity for guys to break through. I think the transition from Whistling Straits (2021) into Rome was fantastic and I think that only strengthened into solidifying some of those players that stepped into that role at Bethpage.

There are so many good young players, like the Højgaards [Nicolai and Rasmus], Ludvig [Åberg], even Bob [MacIntyre]. Those guys are now real stalwarts of the team. There has been a great transition in Europe, so we can afford another new batch of youngsters."

Could consistency be key again for Team Europe?

Europe carried 11 of their 12-man line-up and four of the five vice-captains from their 2023 victory to New York in 2025, with the Molinari brothers - Edoardo and Francesco - already confirmed for a third consecutive stint in Donald's backroom team.

Padraig Harrington has been added as a vice-captain on home soil, while McIlroy anticipates the bulk of Donald's last two teams to be back together again in Ireland.

"If there's ever a place to blend rookies, it is in Europe," McIlroy told Sky Sports . "The thing that I preach around the European Ryder Cup team is there's this continuity.

"I think continuity between the captain, the players, the vice captains is a big thing in a team environment. Look, inevitably there might be some new faces on that team, but I don't think there's certainly not going to be wholesale changes.

"I think the nucleus of our team will remain the nucleus. You might have a couple [new] maybe, but I'd say for the most part, as long as everyone plays well and stays injury-free, you're going to have a very similar looking team to what we've had the last couple."

The Ryder Cup will be held from September 17-19 next year, live on Sky Sports . Donald will be looking to be the first captain in history to win three consecutive Ryder Cups.

articles.title: Vikings news: Brian Flores makes eye-opening take on Week 2 Bears showdown
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings defense faces an early-season trial by fire in Week 2, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is embracing every second of the challeng...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings defense faces an early-season trial by fire in Week 2, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is embracing every second of the challenge. Following a thrilling 39-22 comeback victory over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, Minnesota now turns its attention to an explosive Chicago Bears offense led by head coach Ben Johnson.

Coming off a historic Week 1 scoring exhibition, Chicago poses a stern test for Minnesota's aggressive, blitz-heavy defensive scheme. Speaking to reporters ahead of the high-stakes NFC North showdown, Flores acknowledged the intricate chess match awaiting his group.

"It's a major challenge, and that's what we all signed up for," Flores said on matching up against Johnson's versatile offense.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Flores noted that going from Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur in Week 1 to Johnson in Week 2 keeps his defensive unit on high alert. Johnson's playbook features an array of heavy run packages, run-pass options, and spread concepts, forcing opposing defenses to adjust constantly on the fly.

Chicago certainly validated Flores' caution by dropping 59 points and 552 total yards in a 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers . Quarterback Caleb Williams delivered four total touchdowns, throwing for 269 yards and rushing for 65 yards, while running back D'Andre Swift rushed for 124 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Kyle Monangai added 100 yards on the ground, highlighted by a 61-yard touchdown run. Meanwhile, Flores' unit showed elite adjustments against Green Bay, holding the Packers scoreless over the final 22 minutes while engineering a 29-0 closing run to snatch victory.

Now, Flores must dial up another defensive masterclass at home to slow down Williams and company . Chicago and Minnesota split their intense rivalry series last season, with both contests coming down to nail-biting three-point margins late in the fourth quarter. If Flores can disrupt Johnson's high-powered rhythm on Sunday, the Vikings will secure a pivotal early-season division win and keep their momentum rolling.
